versions.question: With $u=f(x)$ and $dv=g(x)\,dx$, which pair of quantities must be computed before applying the formula?

versions.question: Evaluate $\int x^{2}e^{-3x}\,dx$.
versions.answer:
Let $u=x^2$, $dv=e^{-3x}dx$, so $du=2x\,dx$, $v=-\frac13e^{-3x}$.
$\int x^2e^{-3x}dx=-\frac{x^2}3e^{-3x}+\frac23\int xe^{-3x}dx$
Now $u=x$, $v=-\frac13e^{-3x}$: $\int xe^{-3x}dx=-\frac x3e^{-3x}-\frac19e^{-3x}$.
Hence $\int x^2e^{-3x}dx=-e^{-3x}\left(\frac{x^2}3+\frac{2x}9+\frac2{27}\right)+C$.

versions.question: Evaluate $\int e^{3x}\sin2x\,dx$.
versions.answer:
Let $I=\int e^{3x}\sin2x\,dx$. Take $u=\sin2x$, $dv=e^{3x}dx$: $I=\frac13e^{3x}\sin2x-\frac23\int e^{3x}\cos2x\,dx$.
Take $u=\cos2x$, $dv=e^{3x}dx$: $\int e^{3x}\cos2x\,dx=\frac13e^{3x}\cos2x+\frac23I$.
So $I=\frac13e^{3x}\sin2x-\frac29e^{3x}\cos2x-\frac49I$, hence $\frac{13}9I=\frac19e^{3x}(3\sin2x-2\cos2x)$.
$I=\frac{e^{3x}}{13}(3\sin2x-2\cos2x)+C$.
